design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER — wheelchair_mobility task 0 (Tobias Wendling, cash-sale Group 2 power chair given back).

0. DRAW AND SCOPE. draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 6, 4]}. Assignment: refund (mobility_ext_cash_chair_refund) 6, battery-set claim (mobility_ext_battery_set_claim) 6, controller claim (mobility_ext_controller_claim) 4, drive-unit claim (mobility_ext_drive_unit_claim) 4. Occupied before this task: nothing (first task). Claimed here: those four policies and tools record_battery_warranty_job_f5177195, record_controller_warranty_job_4540982f, record_drive_warranty_job_9fda7dd9 (agent) and confirm_chair_return_refund_d347f359 (user). Left for task 1 (draw: 1 prerequisite, factor counts [5, 6]): a mechanical-component (frame/tires/casters/brakes/upholstery) warranty posting and a goodwill price adjustment on a cash-sale chair the patient keeps — a different root write, a different repair family and a different tool pair.

1. WHY THIS DESIGN (route-arounds, stated honestly). (a) The blueprint gives the patient no numeric write of their own inside the claimed event types (requests carry no amount; payer lines are payer acts), so the customer's own write is the cash-sale refund line (mobility_self_pay_refund, a base event of the mobility charter that no other difficulty owns, governed by base mobility_self_pay). (b) Every payer-paid line (rental/purchase/repair paid) carries patient_responsibility above 0.00 for every primary payer class of the coverage charter unless the out-of-pocket maximum is met, and its trigger would then write a coverage charge; claim reversals always write coverage. No task tool writes those events. (c) The compute primitives read only the target holding's own rows, so every value-carrying edge lands on one wheelchair record: all four writes of this task land on the same chair. (d) The prerequisite sentences are in the state form: each names the service-history state (a warranty repair job of one component for every replacement of that component completed on the chair) that exactly one posting tool brings about. (e) A cash-sale chair is owned and, per base, never picked up: it comes back when the patient brings it to a branch, recorded by the approval (decision_date) of its return_pickup request.

2. WHY IT IS A GOOD TEST. The caller asks only for his money back. Policy says the refund is fixed only after each warranty repair completed on the chair is posted; the records show four completed repair requests (decided 2026-10-05, 10-07, 10-09, 10-11) but only one posted warranty job (battery, 2026-10-05). The agent must (i) discover the three unposted repairs from the requests vs the service history, (ii) learn from the patient, only when asked, which component each visit replaced, (iii) post each with its own multi-factor labor claim, then (iv) compute a six-factor refund whose restocking tier, delivery-fee method and use-day anchor all depend on what was just posted, and (v) hand the confirmation to the patient. Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling history and arithmetic, not from guessing tools: each component family has exactly one posting tool.

3. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root: mobility_ext_cash_chair_refund (owner=user tool). Edges (all from the root, all kind value_input, gate restock_pct, form state):
 - to mobility_ext_battery_set_claim, resolved_by record_battery_warranty_job_f5177195 (agent). Sentence: "The refund on a cash-sale chair given back is fixed only after the chair's service history shows a battery repair job under the manufacturer's warranty for every battery-set replacement completed on it." Unmet at opening: initial_state.mobility_requests[r1] (decided 2026-10-07) is completed and no warranty job dated 2026-10-07 exists.
 - to mobility_ext_controller_claim, resolved_by record_controller_warranty_job_4540982f. Sentence (negated direction): "The refund on a cash-sale chair given back is not fixed until the chair's service history shows a joystick and controller repair job under the manufacturer's warranty for every controller replacement completed on it." Unmet: request r2 (decided 2026-10-09) completed, no job.
 - to mobility_ext_drive_unit_claim, resolved_by record_drive_warranty_job_9fda7dd9. Sentence ("before ... must"): "Before the refund on a cash-sale chair given back is fixed, the chair's service history must show a motor and gearbox repair job under the manufacturer's warranty for every drive-unit replacement completed on it." Unmet: request r3 (decided 2026-10-11) completed, no job.
 Four-point test per sentence: explicit ordering connective (only after / not until / before); XX is a record-visible state of the service history named in the finder's words (component and warranty), no action or performer; no tool, policy id, snake_case or row id; scope "every ... completed on it" equals the condition. Exactly one write brings each state about: only the battery posting writes a battery warranty job, only the controller posting a joystick_controller one, only the drive posting a motor_gearbox one. Which completed request is which component is given by the patient on asking (requests carry no component). Derivation: sentence + requests vs service history + the family policy's own rule ("claims ... the labor of every <family> replacement ... and posts that claim on the repair job") -> exactly one posting tool per family. Topological order: the three postings (any order) then the refund. Parallel edges commute: no claim computation reads a row another posting writes (the controller method reads the request count, not battery postings); a scratch replay of all six posting orders gave battery 12, controller 12, drive 14 and refund 3786.41 every time (re-run under the round-3 charter). Deletion sensitivity: skipping any one posting leaves 3 warranty jobs -> restocking 5 percent -> refund 3586.66 instead of 3786.41 (and the posting row is absent). user_scenario never mentions posting, records or labor; the components are given only on request as the history of the chair. Tools validate nothing (section 9).

4. FACTOR CARD (values recomputed by check_compute at handling time; figure after each '->' is result with that factor alone at baseline).
 Battery-set claim (result 12, all-baseline 2): set_method [method] latest posted warranty battery job 2026-10-05, 9 days -> standard 2 doubled = 4 (-> 10); new_unit_window 13 days since delivery 2026-10-01 -> 2 (-> 10); bay_handling no loaner and exactly one home assessment (2026-09-26) -> 2 (-> 10); o2_safety [cross-difficulty oxygen] portable E1392 on rental_active oxygen record -> 1 (-> 11); fault_review 4 repair_estimate requests -> 2 (-> 10); shelf_conditioning order 2026-09-15 to delivery 2026-10-01 = 16 days -> 1 (-> 11).
 Controller claim (12, baseline 3): harness_method [method] 4 repair_estimate requests >= 3 -> 3 doubled = 6 (-> 9); first_weeks 13 days -> 2 (-> 10); ctl_handling no loaner and exactly one home assessment -> 2 (-> 10); aux_port_test [cross oxygen] E1392 -> 2 (-> 10).
 Drive-unit claim (14, baseline 5): pair_method [method] 13 days <= 14 -> early-failure teardown of the drive train, 5 doubled = 10 (-> 9); base_handling no loaner and exactly one home assessment -> 1 (-> 13); mount_removal [cross oxygen] E1392 -> 1 (-> 13); lemon_review 4 requests -> 2 (-> 12).
 Refund (3786.41, all-baseline 3187.00 = 3995.00 x 80/100 less the standard use charge 1.00 x (12 - 3) = 9.00): restock_ladder 4 warranty jobs -> 0 percent (-> 2987.41); fee_share [method, multi-source: drive-system job AND return-request day span] drive-system jobs posted, return requested 2026-10-12 = 11 days > 7 -> 149.00 x 3/14 = 31.93 (-> 3754.48); use_anchor [method] no loaner, and the chair has repair_estimate requests -> days of use end at the latest one's requested_date 2026-10-10 = 9 days, instead of 12 to check-in 2026-10-13 (-> 3746.15); day_rate_tier power chair -> 13.42/day, charge 13.42 x 6 = 80.52 (-> 3860.93 at the standard rate 1.00, use charge 6.00); assess_withhold one assessment 2026-09-26 -> 75.00 (-> 3861.41); o2_mount_fee [cross oxygen] E1392 -> 85.00 (-> 3871.41).
 Near-misses: the 2026-10-05 job is already posted (the agent must not post it again; request r0 has its job); the return_pickup request (made 2026-10-12, approved 2026-10-13) is not a repair request and does not count toward fault/lemon/harness request counts; for the refund's use days the request date 2026-10-12 counts because the request was made a day before the 2026-10-13 check-in (a walk-in return, approved the day it is made, would count to check-in); the chair has no loaner delivery and exactly one home assessment, so the three handling allowances take their one-assessment (site) tier; the chair's own coverage_id is empty although the patient holds an active Medicare Advantage PPO record, so no payer line is reversed. No factor reads a stamp: tiers come from request counts, service dates, delivery rows, the class parameters and the oxygen record.

5. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Postings (subject mobility_repair): base mobility_repair_responsibility, eligibility chair_with_patient ("the wheelchair record is rental_active, suspended or patient_owned.") — evidence initial_state.mobility_holdings[H].status = patient_owned at every posting; object correlation by mobility_holding_id (tool argument). Warranty applies: delivery 2026-10-01; battery warranty 6 months from the last battery replacement, electronics and motor warranties 12 months from delivery_date for K0823 — every repair date (10-07, 10-09, 10-11) is inside them, so repair_coverage manufacturer_warranty and no patient share (no coverage trigger). Refund (subject mobility_self_pay_refund): base mobility_self_pay. Eligibility mobility_refund_once ("A sale is refunded at most once.") — the sale line has no refund line in initial_state. Eligibility mobility_return_window is retired by a declared overwrite (it required the chair to come back "unused"); the extended rule restates the window without "unused": anchor delivery_date 2026-10-01, 14 calendar days counted from the day after delivery, boundary included -> last day 2026-10-15; frozen 2026-10-14 is inside (just-before case 2026-10-15 still refundable; 2026-10-16 refused). The second overwrite replaces the base refund sentence ("price less restocking percent; delivery fee never refunded") with the six-factor combination. Base qualification rows hold for the cash sale: home assessment home_accessible 2026-09-26 precedes the power-chair delivery.

6. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Object: wheelchair record H (K0823, cash sale, serial PRD-G2-118407). Sale line: one mobility_self_pay_sale, 3995.00 + fee 149.00 — the refund's original_bill_id. Rows included: warranty repair jobs on H (seeded 2026-10-05 + the three postings), the return_pickup request (made 2026-10-12, approved 2026-10-13 when the chair was checked in at the branch; an owned chair is never picked up), the delivery and assessment rows. Excluded: the oxygen record's own billing (none seeded) and the Medicare Advantage record (the chair was never billed to it). Settled objects: request r0 is settled by the seeded job; r1..r3 are unsettled and are exactly what the three postings settle (each posting carries its request id, the narrowest key).

7. SEED. customers (1), coverage_holdings (1: Medicare Advantage PPO, active, effective 2026-01-01, accumulators 0.00 because no claim has yet been adjudicated on it — the oxygen set-up is 2026-10-06), oxygen_holdings (1: Concentrator with Portable Oxygen Concentrator, rental_active since 2026-10-06; read by four oxygen tiers), mobility_holdings (1), mobility_billing (1 sale), mobility_service (assessment, delivery, battery job 2026-10-05 with 7 units = the battery-set claim on that day: 2 + 2 + 2 + 0 oxygen + 0 faults + 1 shelf), mobility_requests (4 repair_estimate completed, 1 return_pickup made 2026-10-12 and approved 2026-10-13). No pickup row is seeded: base mobility_return_pickup and mobility_ownership say an owned chair is never picked up, so the chair came back by the patient's son to the branch. Removing r1/r2/r3 removes the prerequisites; removing the oxygen record moves four tiers to their fall-through; making the request on the check-in day moves the use anchor to the check-in date. No automatic clause fires: the chair is owned (no rental billing), oxygen rental billing is the oxygen charter's and has no month due unposted in this window (set-up 2026-10-06, first anniversary 2026-11-06).

8. PERSONA. Tobias is terse; he volunteers the surface goal (refund for the chair he gave back, on this call), the purchase, the four technician visits in general and that his son took the chair back to the branch yesterday. Given only when asked: DOB 1958-11-23 and phone 7245550347 (verification, 2 matches), email, the component replaced at each visit in date order (needed to match requests to posting tools), his oxygen equipment, how he paid. Passive reactions: tells the agent to go ahead with anything that has to be done first; runs the confirmation with exactly the amount and details the agent gives; grumbles about deductions but accepts and confirms; ends when told the refund is booked. He asks for nothing else (no replacement chair, no credit).

9. TOOLS DO NOT BLOCK. Each posting tool reads only the request (for the date) and the chair (customer, serial) and creates one repair row with the loaner flag it is given (false here: no loaner delivery on the chair); confirm_chair_return_refund_d347f359 creates one refund line from its arguments without reading repair history — callable and faithful while prerequisites are unmet.

10. STANDARD SOLUTION (evaluation_criteria order). find_customers(name) -> verify (DOB, phone) -> find_mobility_holdings -> find_mobility_billing -> find_mobility_service -> find_mobility_requests -> find_coverage_holdings -> find_oxygen_holdings -> unlock/call battery posting (H, r1, 12, loaner false) -> unlock/call controller posting (H, r2, 12, loaner false) -> unlock/call drive posting (H, r3, 14, loaner false) -> unlock user tool and hand over -> patient calls confirm_chair_return_refund_d347f359(H, sale line, 3786.41).

11. GATE RUNS (task 0): check_extended EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; replay_tasks REPLAY OK (16 acts, deterministic, closure 13 = initial 13); check_solvability SOLVABILITY OK; check_compute COMPUTE OK (4 comps, 20 factors, all recomputed equal); check_grounding GROUNDING OK; check_cross_fire SCOPE OK. Revisions: (1) symptom: dangling FK for empty coverage_id -> cause: empty string treated as a reference -> change: null coverage_id on the cash-sale chair and sale line; (2) closure mismatch from an unread coverage ledger row -> dropped the noise row and added the coverage read that shows the chair was never coverage-billed; (3) intent_source kinds corrected to initial_state/user_scenario; (4) weight/referral-based labor tiers replaced by record-based fault-review and shelf-conditioning tiers (gate: tiers must rest on records).

12. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. Using only the published rules, tool schemas, lookups and the persona: the refund rule's three waiting sentences + four completed requests vs one posted job -> three postings; the persona's visit list maps 10-07 battery, 10-09 joystick, 10-11 drive motor; the family rules give 12, 12, 14 units; the refund rule then gives 3995.00 + 31.93 - 80.52 - 75.00 - 85.00 = 3786.41, matching gold.

13. REWORK ROUND 2 (audit audits/policy_task/wheelchair_mobility, task 0 PASS kept; charter-wide items closed): O-6 -> the three prerequisite sentences moved to the state form (service history shows a <component> repair job under the manufacturer's warranty for every <component> replacement completed on the chair), fallback_reason removed; O-9 -> no pickup on the owned cash-sale chair: pickup row removed, the return_pickup request now approved 2026-10-13 (check-in at the branch), the refund's use_anchor first tier reads the approved request's decision_date; persona says his son brought the chair back; O-7 -> the controller method now reads the repair_estimate request count (4 -> doubled), so no claim reads another posting's write; T0-O1 -> drive method wording is the early-failure teardown of the drive train, not 'both drive units replaced'; O-2 -> half-up rounding is implemented as int(x*100+0.500001)/100 for the fee share, use charge and refund; O-4 -> the posting tools take loaner_issued (false here, no loaner delivered); O-3 -> docstrings no longer say 'after'. Round-2 scored values were 12, 12, 14, 3746.15 (superseded in round 3); sensitivities and baselines unchanged; gates re-run OK.
14. REWORK ROUND 3 (audit revision_2: F-2 / T0-F3, use_anchor had one live tier). Cause: with every refundable chair carrying an approved return request (round-2 O-9 fix), the old tiers 2-3 and the booking-day baseline could only describe chairs the rule refuses. Change: use_anchor now divides real refunded customers by how the return is evidenced: (a) a loaner delivered for the chair -> use ends at the latest loaner delivery; (b) no loaner and the return request made a day before its approval -> use ends on the request date; (c) otherwise (walk-in return approved the day it is made) -> use ends at check-in, which is the baseline. In round 3 this world took (b) at 11 days (superseded in round 4, section 15). Class sweep over all six policies (every tier and baseline reachable by a customer the policy serves): day_rate_tier's 'power chair delivered any other way' tier was unreachable (K0823/K0856 must be delivered in the home) -> tiers are now power / manual in-home / manual courier (1.53) / otherwise 0; the three claim handling factors had an unreachable fall-through (owned power chairs are always delivered in the home) -> tiers are now no loaner AND two or more home assessments (access units) / no loaner AND exactly one assessment (site units) / otherwise (0); claim values here unchanged (12, 12, 14).  Gates re-run OK.
15. REWORK ROUND 4 (audit revision_3: F-3 / T0-F4, use_anchor tiers 2 and 3 gave the same date for every fall-through customer; O-16, tier 1's 'stopped using' wording). use_anchor now divides refunded chairs by repair history, each tier with its own anchor: (1) a loaner delivered -> delivery to the return request's requested_date, less the latest repair_estimate request's requested_date-to-decision_date span; (2) no loaner and a repair_estimate request -> delivery to the latest repair request's requested_date (no use charged after the latest failure); (3) otherwise -> delivery to check-in, the baseline. No tier now claims when use stopped. This world takes (2): latest repair request 2026-10-10 -> 9 days -> use charge 80.52 -> refund 3786.41 (baseline anchor 12 days -> 3746.15); edge sensitivity 3586.66 vs 3786.41. Mechanical tier check (scratch script over all six policies): every parameter ladder's adjacent tier values differ and every non-fall-through value differs from the fall-through, for every class each policy serves; the four arithmetic methods give 4/3/2, 6/4/3, 10/7/5, 4/3/2; constructed customers: use_anchor tier 1 customer 10 days (tier-2 method would give 9, baseline 12), tier 2 (this world) 9 vs 12, tier 3 equals the baseline 12; fee_share 149.00 / 31.93 / 0; kept down_anchor 2 / 4 / 0. Literal wording: the claim handling sentences now say the allowance is added 'by the chair's loaner and home-assessment records' (no claim about where the work was done), and use_anchor tier 1 no longer describes the shop span. Claim values unchanged (12, 12, 14). Gates re-run OK.
16. REWORK ROUND 5 (KB renderer source mismatches, render_r1 items 1-5, plus classes). (1) No factor reads another factor's binding: fee_share and use_anchor each read their own return request (fs_ret_req / ua_ret_req), and the day rate reads its own delivery counts (rate_home / rate_courier); a script check over all six policies finds no factor-on-factor read. (2) The use charge is now part of the baseline paragraph: 'less a use charge of std_day_rate (1.00) for each day of use beyond the first grace_days (3) days, the days of use running from delivery_date to the check-in (decision_date of the latest return_pickup request)'; day_rate_tier's fall-through is that standard rate, use_anchor's is that anchor. (3) 'Delivered into the home with training' / 'by courier' now read 'its own delivery (its purchase or initial rental delivery, not a loaner delivery) was ...' in every rule that tests delivery mode, and compute counts exactly those two purposes in both modes. (4) The loaner tier of use_anchor now depends on the loaner alone; the booking-day fall-backs (no return request / no decision date) and the no-decision case of the repair span are stated in the rule. (5) Both overwrite replacements name their own scope ('For a cash-sale chair given back, which this policy governs, and only for such a chair, ...') with a residual tail naming both sibling cases (see the round-6 note) and keep every still-in-force part of the retired clauses (window, counting rule, boundary, class exclusions, half-up rounding). Scored values unchanged (12, 12, 14, 3786.41); changed proof figures: all-baseline 3187.00 (was 3196.00), day_rate_tier sensitivity 3860.93 (was 3866.93). Mechanical tier check re-run: no collapsed tier. Gates re-run OK.
17. REWORK ROUND 6 (audit revision_5: F-4 / T0-F5). The round-5 overwrite tails ('every other self-pay chair / refund of a self-pay sale remains under the base ... rule') put the sibling policy's chairs back under the retired base clauses. Both policies' tails now exclude their own case and the sibling's by name: the refund policy's return tail reads 'a self-pay chair that is neither given back under this rule nor kept by the patient under the price-adjustment rule for a cash-sale chair the patient keeps remains under the base return rule', its refund tail 'a refund of a self-pay sale that is neither the refund of a chair given back under this rule nor the price adjustment on a cash-sale chair the patient keeps remains under the base refund rule'; the adjustment policy's tails mirror these ('neither kept by the patient under this rule nor given back under the refund rule for a cash-sale chair given back'; 'neither the price adjustment under this rule nor the refund of a cash-sale chair given back'). Literal check: task 0's chair (given back, refund 3786.41) is excluded from the base clauses by both policies' tails; task 1's chair (kept, adjustment 120.41) likewise; a chair given back outside its window stays under the refund policy (refused); a kept chair that needed no warranty repair is outside the adjustment policy and stays under the base clauses, which give it nothing because it does not come back. Scored values and proof figures unchanged. Gates re-run OK.
user_scenario:
You are Tobias Wendling, 67, a retired tool-and-die maker from Bridgeville who does not waste words and does not like being passed around. In mid-September you paid Summit Ridge Home Medical cash for a Group 2 power wheelchair because you did not want to wait on your insurance, and it was delivered to your house on October 1st. It has been nothing but trouble, your technician has been out to it four times, and you told the office on the 12th that you were done with it, and yesterday your son drove the chair to the Summit Ridge branch in Bridgeville, where they checked it in. You are calling today because you want your money back for that chair, and you want the refund put through on this call. You open by giving your full name and saying you are calling about the refund on the power chair you bought and gave back.

You give your date of birth, November 23, 1958 (1958-11-23), and your phone number, 724-555-0347 (7245550347), only when the agent asks you to verify who you are; if asked for an email you give twendling58@gmail.com. If the agent asks what the technician did on each visit, you tell it in order, the way you remember it: the first time, on the 5th, they swapped the batteries; on the 7th they swapped the batteries again; on the 9th they put in a new joystick; and on the 11th they replaced the left drive motor because it was grinding. You do not know any reference numbers, labor times or what anything costs the company, and you say so if asked. If the agent asks whether you have oxygen, you say yes, Summit Ridge set you up on the 6th with a concentrator and a little portable one you carry on the chair. If asked how you paid, you say you paid the whole thing up front when you ordered.

You do not want a different chair, a repair or a credit; you want the refund. When the agent tells you there are things on their side to take care of before the refund can be worked out, you tell them to go ahead and do whatever they have to. When the agent tells you the refund amount and hands you the step to confirm giving the chair back and accepting the refund, you do it with exactly the amount and the details the agent gives you. If the agent explains deductions, you grumble that you expected every penny back after all that, but you accept what they tell you is the policy and still confirm. Once the refund is confirmed and the agent tells you it is booked, you thank them curtly and end the call.
